plan_areas.community_vision: By embracing its rich Chesapeake culture and heritage, invaluable ecosystems and emerging opportunities, Anne Arundel County embodies the best of both the past and future, providing its residents a place where all are proud to live, work, learn, and play.

In the coming years, Annapolis will be a more equitable, healthy, and resilient city. It will be a more walkable and connected city where multiple safe and reliable transportation options reduce personal vehicle dependency. It will be a city which prioritizes public investments in its most socially vulnerable communities; a city which expands housing options accessible to residents of all income levels; and a city which grows a community of diverse local entrepreneurs aided by inclusive economic programs and opportunities. Annapolis will be a city which prioritizes the preservation, restoration, maintenance, and enhancement of its natural resources, particularly when planning for new development. It will be a city which ensures that all residents have access to high quality recreational amenities particularly public water access; and it will be a city which values its cultural life through support for arts initiatives, artists and arts organizations, and citywide historic preservation efforts. And Annapolis will be climate ready. Its infrastructure will be designed to withstand or adapt to the impacts from climate change. The city will protect its communities and institutions most at risk of climate impacts; and the city will reduce its carbon emissions through a variety of coordinated policies, programs, and investments.

A multi-year investment strategy – a strategic set of revitalization initiatives and projects that local partners believe will increase the economic vitality and livability of their community, increase prosperity for local households and improve the health of the surrounding environment.

plan_quotes.text: Much of North County is a food desert, with few locations where healthy food can be purchased.

plan_quotes.text: Approximately 75,000 (13.2%) County residents live in an area categorized as a food desert, which is an urban neighborhood or rural town without ready access to fresh, healthy and affordable food.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 Plan2040 for Anne Arundel County highlights a significant statistic that, "Approximately 75,000 (13.2%) County residents live in an area categorized as a food desert, which is an urban neighborhood or rural town without ready access to fresh, healthy and affordable food."

plan_quotes.text: Work with local employers to provide job training and readiness programs as well as support services such as childcare and transportation to ensure residents can take advantage of employment opportunities in the County.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 Plan2040 for Anne Arundel County identifies a strategy to, "Work with local employers to provide job training and readiness programs as well as support services such as childcare and transportation to ensure residents can take advantage of employment opportunities in the County."

plan_quotes.text: One area of the city classified as a food desert by the USDA according to 2019 data is the Eastport neighborhood between Tyler Avenue/Hilltop Lane and Adams Street to the west of Bay Ridge Avenue, where there is a high rate of poverty for the region, low vehicle access, and poor proximity to supermarkets.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Annapolis Ahead Comprehensive Plan 2040 identifies that, "One area of the city classified as a food desert by the USDA...is the Eastport neighborhood...where there is a high rate of poverty for the region, low vehicle access, and poor proximity to supermarkets."

plan_quotes.text: A small grocery should be included in future redevelopment to address a well-documented gap in food access.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Annapolis Ahead Comprehensive Plan 2040 notes the need for a grocery store in Eastport, stating that, "A small grocery should be included in future redevelopment to address a well-documented gap in food access."

plan_quotes.text: Efforts should be made to broaden the reach of the farmers’ markets to communities with a documented need for improved access to healthy food.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Annapolis Ahead Comprehensive Plan 2040 recommends that, "Efforts should be made to broaden the reach of the farmers’ markets to communities with a documented need for improved access to healthy food."

plan_quotes.text: The City is also looking to address access to healthy foods and eliminate an existing food desert within the Sustainable Community area. Land use limitations have proven to be a challenge to this effort but a new focus on creating a food cooperative that would require a smaller development footprint than a conventional grocery is gaining momentum.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 City of Annapolis Sustainable Communities Renewal Application notes the city is looking to "address access to healthy foods and eliminate an existing food desert within the Sustainable Community area," with a new focus on creating a food cooperative.

plan_quotes.text: Similar to the previous Sustainable Communities renewal, food deserts are still a concentrated issue within Annapolis that have yet to be eliminated within a portion of the city.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 City of Annapolis Sustainable Communities Renewal Application highlights an ongoing need, stating that "food deserts are still a concentrated issue within Annapolis that have yet to be eliminated within a portion of the city."

plan_quotes.text: Well-documented food desert
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key challenge identified in the 2024 City of Annapolis Sustainable Communities Renewal Application is the presence of a "Well-documented food desert."

plan_quotes.text: Coordinate retail strategy as part of the Eastport CNI project to ensure a small grocery or other healthy food provider is part of the redevelopment.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: To address food deserts, the 2024 City of Annapolis Sustainable Communities Renewal Application proposes a strategy to "ensure a small grocery or other healthy food provider is part of the redevelopment" of the Eastport community.

plan_areas.community_vision: Thrive Montgomery 2050 aims to create communities that offer equitable access to jobs, more housing, transportation, parks, and public spaces. Just as importantly, it can help guide the design of the built environment to strengthen the social and physical health of our residents, supporting active lifestyles and encouraging interaction and engagement.

plan_quotes.text: As the county plans for the future, it should continue to find ways to address the specific needs of the vulnerable populations impacted by the hidden costs of poverty and determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan observes the need to "determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation."

plan_quotes.text: Improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan highlights the need to "improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism."

plan_quotes.text: Likewise, community gardens help to reduce the impact of food deserts in low-income areas, encourage physical activity and social interaction, and give residents who do not have yards access to nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy lifestyle.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan notes that, "community gardens help to reduce the impact of food deserts in low-income areas... and give residents who do not have yards access to nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy lifestyle."

plan_areas.community_vision: Howard County is a welcoming and inclusive community that residents are proud to call home. Our collective vision is to accommodate future growth in a manner that retains and improves upon the unique and diverse community character of Howard County. We will continue to support, promote, and act toward creating a community grounded in civility, sustainable development patterns, environmental stewardship, and well-maintained supporting infrastructure. Policies and investments will respect and prioritize the natural environment, historic resources and agricultural heritage, diverse cultures and people, and established community character in an equitable, predictable, sustainable, and achievable way for generations to come.

plan_quotes.text: Some participants advocated for more food options located closer to carless households. Columbia’s walkable village centers were identified as good locations for restaurants and grocery stores featuring locally-sourced food.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The HoCo By Design plan notes a community desire for "more food options located closer to carless households," identifying Columbia’s walkable village centers as good locations for restaurants and grocery stores featuring locally-sourced food.

plan_quotes.text: Use creative solutions to address food deserts (areas without healthy, fresh food options).
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key finding from community focus groups in the HoCo By Design plan is the need to "use creative solutions to address food deserts (areas without healthy, fresh food options)."

plan_quotes.text: Sustainability and food security mean preservation of our local farms and pollinators.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A resident's perspective in the HoCo By Design plan links environmental health to food systems, stating that, "Sustainability and food security mean preservation of our local farms and pollinators."

plan_quotes.text: To ensure underserved populations can participate in training, entities involved in workforce development should partner to offer resources such as child care.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The HoCo By Design plan highlights that to support economic opportunity, "entities involved in workforce development should partner to offer resources such as child care" to ensure underserved populations can participate in training.

A unique geologic landform in Maryland, Sugarloaf Mountain is a defining element of Frederick County’s treasured scenic and rural landscape. The mountain and the area surrounding it possess a sublime beauty and significant biodiversity, where a high-quality environment is maintained. Forestlands, aquatic resources, wildlife habitat, inspiring vistas, and historic resources are valued and protected. Land uses are sensitive to both the natural environment and rural character of the area. Stewardship of the area’s natural assets and cultural resources ensures healthy, resilient, and economically productive lands for current and future generations. As we face climate change challenges, Sugarloaf Mountain and the surrounding landscape provide ecosystem benefits to the residents of both Frederick County and the wider region, enhancing the sustainability of our shared environment.

In the coming years, Annapolis will be a more equitable, healthy, and resilient city. It will be a more walkable and connected city where multiple safe and reliable transportation options reduce personal vehicle dependency. It will be a city which prioritizes public investments in its most socially vulnerable communities; a city which expands housing options accessible to residents of all income levels; and a city which grows a community of diverse local entrepreneurs aided by inclusive economic programs and opportunities. Annapolis will be a city which prioritizes the preservation, restoration, maintenance, and enhancement of its natural resources, particularly when planning for new development. It will be a city which ensures that all residents have access to high quality recreational amenities particularly public water access; and it will be a city which values its cultural life through support for arts initiatives, artists and arts organizations, and citywide historic preservation efforts. And Annapolis will be climate ready. Its infrastructure will be designed to withstand or adapt to the impacts from climate change. The city will protect its communities and institutions most at risk of climate impacts; and the city will reduce its carbon emissions through a variety of coordinated policies, programs, and investments.

plan_areas.community_vision: By embracing its rich Chesapeake culture and heritage, invaluable ecosystems and emerging opportunities, Anne Arundel County embodies the best of both the past and future, providing its residents a place where all are proud to live, work, learn, and play.

In the coming years, Annapolis will be a more equitable, healthy, and resilient city. It will be a more walkable and connected city where multiple safe and reliable transportation options reduce personal vehicle dependency. It will be a city which prioritizes public investments in its most socially vulnerable communities; a city which expands housing options accessible to residents of all income levels; and a city which grows a community of diverse local entrepreneurs aided by inclusive economic programs and opportunities. Annapolis will be a city which prioritizes the preservation, restoration, maintenance, and enhancement of its natural resources, particularly when planning for new development. It will be a city which ensures that all residents have access to high quality recreational amenities particularly public water access; and it will be a city which values its cultural life through support for arts initiatives, artists and arts organizations, and citywide historic preservation efforts. And Annapolis will be climate ready. Its infrastructure will be designed to withstand or adapt to the impacts from climate change. The city will protect its communities and institutions most at risk of climate impacts; and the city will reduce its carbon emissions through a variety of coordinated policies, programs, and investments.

plan_areas.community_vision: Through numerous public meetings, research and data collection and discussions with people who have worked diligently to improve Allegany County, a picture of this area has more clearly come into focus; the key theme of this portrait centers upon improved vitality, economic health and enhanced livability. This picture includes removal of blight and supporting infill development, economic development concentrated in or around existing municipalities, eco-tourism resulting from new trail extensions and connectivity, preservation of sensitive and critical areas, investment and citizen pride in Allegany County.
Cumberland’s focus on providing a great place to live and a supportive place to build a profitable business to be realized through a comprehensive approach.

plan_quotes.text: Availability of quality childcare is an important factor in the County’s economy and quality of life. According to Maryland Child Care Network-Child Care Demographics 2012, the following data for Allegany County was reported: Family Child Care Providers: 73 with a capacity for 550 children. Child Care Centers (8-12 hours): 17 with a capacity for 1,037 children.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2014 Allegany County Comprehensive Plan highlights that, "Availability of quality childcare is an important factor in the County’s economy and quality of life." The plan references 2012 data indicating the county had 73 Family Child Care Providers with a capacity for 550 children and 17 Child Care Centers with a capacity for 1,037 children.

It meets the diverse needs of all Prince Georgians and embraces and builds on the momentum generated by new residents, technology, and business opportunities.

plan_areas.community_vision: Thrive Montgomery 2050 aims to create communities that offer equitable access to jobs, more housing, transportation, parks, and public spaces. Just as importantly, it can help guide the design of the built environment to strengthen the social and physical health of our residents, supporting active lifestyles and encouraging interaction and engagement.

Thrive Montgomery 2050 strives to create racially integrated and just communities by advancing just planning policies and public investments in underserved communities, promoting the racial and economic integration of neighborhoods, and focusing on the potential for the design of communities to help build social trust and inclusion while encouraging civic participation.

plan_quotes.text: As the county plans for the future, it should continue to find ways to address the specific needs of the vulnerable populations impacted by the hidden costs of poverty and determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan observes the need to "determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation."

plan_quotes.text: Improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan highlights the need to "improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism."

plan_quotes.text: Likewise, community gardens help to reduce the impact of food deserts in low-income areas, encourage physical activity and social interaction, and give residents who do not have yards access to nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy lifestyle.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan notes that, "community gardens help to reduce the impact of food deserts in low-income areas... and give residents who do not have yards access to nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy lifestyle."

plan_quotes.text: Continue DEP’s efforts to reduce wasted food and development of recommendations for a County-wide edible food recovery program. Provide focused education and outreach campaign “Food Is Too Good to Waste” to encourage and motivate residents and businesses to reduce wasted food, conduct focused education to shoppers providing tips to reduce wasted food, and continue research and survey assistance to measure the amount of edible food available for recovery from commercial food establishments.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Montgomery County Sustainable Communities Renewal application outlines a strategy to 'continue research and survey assistance to measure the amount of edible food available for recovery from commercial food establishments.'

plan_quotes.text: Relieve financial stress on farmers and encourage start-up agritourism businesses in/around the County’s 93K-acre Ag Reserve to help increase farm-related profitability, generate additional tourism spending and increase the County’s tax revenue while developing tourism products in the County’s rural areas that are open, accessible and identifiable to the County’s diverse residents and visitors.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key economic goal in the 2023 Montgomery County Sustainable Communities Renewal application is to 'relieve financial stress on farmers and encourage start-up agritourism businesses in/around the County’s 93K-acre Ag Reserve.'

plan_areas.community_vision: Howard County is a welcoming and inclusive community that residents are proud to call home. Our collective vision is to accommodate future growth in a manner that retains and improves upon the unique and diverse community character of Howard County. We will continue to support, promote, and act toward creating a community grounded in civility, sustainable development patterns, environmental stewardship, and well-maintained supporting infrastructure. Policies and investments will respect and prioritize the natural environment, historic resources and agricultural heritage, diverse cultures and people, and established community character in an equitable, predictable, sustainable, and achievable way for generations to come.

plan_quotes.text: Some participants advocated for more food options located closer to carless households. Columbia’s walkable village centers were identified as good locations for restaurants and grocery stores featuring locally-sourced food.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The HoCo By Design plan notes a community desire for "more food options located closer to carless households," identifying Columbia’s walkable village centers as good locations for restaurants and grocery stores featuring locally-sourced food.

plan_quotes.text: Use creative solutions to address food deserts (areas without healthy, fresh food options).
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key finding from community focus groups in the HoCo By Design plan is the need to "use creative solutions to address food deserts (areas without healthy, fresh food options)."

plan_quotes.text: Sustainability and food security mean preservation of our local farms and pollinators.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A resident's perspective in the HoCo By Design plan links environmental health to food systems, stating that, "Sustainability and food security mean preservation of our local farms and pollinators."

plan_quotes.text: To ensure underserved populations can participate in training, entities involved in workforce development should partner to offer resources such as child care.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The HoCo By Design plan highlights that to support economic opportunity, "entities involved in workforce development should partner to offer resources such as child care" to ensure underserved populations can participate in training.

plan_quotes.text: In 2020, Roving Radish, an award-winning Howard County program that provides healthy meal kits sourced from local farms, opened its first storefront in Long Reach Village Center. plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Long Reach Sustainable Community plan highlights a key addition to the community, noting that, 'Roving Radish, an award-winning Howard County program that provides healthy meal kits sourced from local farms, opened its first storefront in Long Reach Village Center.'

plan_quotes.text: In 2020, Howard International Grocer, a market specializing in international foods and halal meat, moved into 1,733 square feet of the Long Reach Village Center, as part of the Long Reach Rising revitalization project led by Howard County. Howard International Grocer sells fresh and frozen meat and fish, fresh vegetables, fruit, milk, eggs, snacks, and more.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Long Reach Sustainable Community plan notes progress in food retail diversity, stating, 'Howard International Grocer, a market specializing in international foods and halal meat, moved into...the Long Reach Village Center...[and] sells fresh and frozen meat and fish, fresh vegetables, fruit, milk, eggs, snacks, and more.'

plan_quotes.text: Head Start, a vital early education program of the Community Action Council of Howard County, moved one of its locations to the Long Reach Village Center in 2020. The Long Reach location has approximately 5,332 square feet, allowing Head Start to increase its capacity from 38 to 80 children. Head Start provides free pre-school to eligible 3 to 5-year-old children.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Long Reach Sustainable Community plan highlights expanded access to early education, stating that a new Head Start location in the Village Center is 'allowing Head Start to increase its capacity from 38 to 80 children.'

plan_areas.community_vision: Howard County is a welcoming and inclusive community that residents are proud to call home. plan_areas.community_vision: Thrive Montgomery 2050 aims to create communities that offer equitable access to jobs, more housing, transportation, parks, and public spaces. Just as importantly, it can help guide the design of the built environment to strengthen the social and physical health of our residents, supporting active lifestyles and encouraging interaction and engagement.

plan_quotes.text: As the county plans for the future, it should continue to find ways to address the specific needs of the vulnerable populations impacted by the hidden costs of poverty and determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan observes the need to "determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation."

plan_quotes.text: Improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan highlights the need to "improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism."

plan_quotes.text: Likewise, community gardens help to reduce the impact of food deserts in low-income areas, encourage physical activity and social interaction, and give residents who do not have yards access to nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy lifestyle.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan notes that, "community gardens help to reduce the impact of food deserts in low-income areas... and give residents who do not have yards access to nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy lifestyle."

plan_areas.community_vision: Rockville will be a vibrant, multicultural, and socio-economically inclusive city with distinct neighborhoods that are supported by a strong local economy, a healthy natural environment, and a desirable quality of life founded on a responsive government.

Thrive Montgomery 2050 aims to create communities that offer equitable access to jobs, more housing, transportation, parks, and public spaces. Just as importantly, it can help guide the design of the built environment to strengthen the social and physical health of our residents, supporting active lifestyles and encouraging interaction and engagement.

plan_quotes.text: Rockville is generally well served by a range of full-service supermarkets and specialty food stores. However residents without access to a car may face challenges, particularly those residents with lower incomes.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 City of Rockville Comprehensive Plan observes that while the city is generally well-served by supermarkets, "residents without access to a car may face challenges, particularly those residents with lower incomes."

plan_quotes.text: Seek opportunities for fresh food and other goods and services for residents of David Scull Courts and other nearby residents and workers.

plan_quotes.text: Residents have indicated concerns about potential adverse impacts of traffic, excessive on-street parking, and noise; and believe that the number and size of child care centers should be limited to preserve the residential character of the neighborhood.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 City of Rockville Comprehensive Plan highlights the community's desire to balance the need for child care with preserving neighborhood character, noting concerns about potential impacts from "traffic, excessive on-street parking, and noise."

plan_quotes.text: Cultivate a local food system that provides residents of all income levels access to healthy fresh food and improves food security.

plan_quotes.text: As the county plans for the future, it should continue to find ways to address the specific needs of the vulnerable populations impacted by the hidden costs of poverty and determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan observes the need to "determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation."

plan_quotes.text: Improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan highlights the need to "improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism."

plan_quotes.text: Likewise, community gardens help to reduce the impact of food deserts in low-income areas, encourage physical activity and social interaction, and give residents who do not have yards access to nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy lifestyle.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan notes that, "community gardens help to reduce the impact of food deserts in low-income areas... and give residents who do not have yards access to nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy lifestyle."

plan_areas.community_vision: In 2035, Prince George’s County is the community of choice for families, businesses, and workers in the region. It is distinguished by strong, green, and healthy communities; a competitive, innovative, and adaptive economy; vibrant and walkable mixed-use centers; quality open space; restored ecosystems; and iconic destinations. It meets the diverse needs of all Prince Georgians and embraces and builds on the momentum generated by new residents, technology, and business opportunities.

plan_quotes.text: Some noted that the costs of childcare and transportation were a barrier to employment as the costs could exceed participants’ earning potential.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2014 Plan Prince George's 2035 notes that for some residents, "the costs of childcare and transportation were a barrier to employment as the costs could exceed participants’ earning potential."

plan_quotes.text: Promote healthy lifestyles by ensuring access to healthy foods, health services, and a network of trails, parks, and recreational opportunities.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2014 Plan Prince George's 2035 outlines a vision for healthy communities that, "Promote healthy lifestyles by ensuring access to healthy foods, health services, and a network of trails, parks, and recreational opportunities."

plan_quotes.text: Approximately 100,000 County residents lived in food deserts in 2010, defined as low-income census tracts where a significant share or number of residents are more than one mile (in urban settings) or ten miles (in rural settings) from the nearest supermarket.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2014 Plan Prince George's 2035 notes a key challenge is that, "Approximately 100,000 County residents lived in food deserts in 2010, defined as low-income census tracts where a significant share or number of residents are more than one mile (in urban settings) or ten miles (in rural settings) from the nearest supermarket."

plan_quotes.text: The majority of food deserts (approximately 73 percent) are concentrated inside the Capital Beltway.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2014 Plan Prince George's 2035 notes that, "The majority of food deserts (approximately 73 percent) are concentrated inside the Capital Beltway."

plan_quotes.text: 71 percent of all restaurants in Prince George’s County were classified in 2012 as fast food.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key community health concern identified in the 2014 Plan Prince George's 2035 is that, "71 percent of all restaurants in Prince George’s County were classified in 2012 as fast food."

plan_areas.community_vision: By embracing its rich Chesapeake culture and heritage, invaluable ecosystems and emerging opportunities, Anne Arundel County embodies the best of both the past and future, providing its residents a place where all are proud to live, work, learn, and play.

In the coming years, Annapolis will be a more equitable, healthy, and resilient city. It will be a more walkable and connected city where multiple safe and reliable transportation options reduce personal vehicle dependency. It will be a city which prioritizes public investments in its most socially vulnerable communities; a city which expands housing options accessible to residents of all income levels; and a city which grows a community of diverse local entrepreneurs aided by inclusive economic programs and opportunities. Annapolis will be a city which prioritizes the preservation, restoration, maintenance, and enhancement of its natural resources, particularly when planning for new development. It will be a city which ensures that all residents have access to high quality recreational amenities particularly public water access; and it will be a city which values its cultural life through support for arts initiatives, artists and arts organizations, and citywide historic preservation efforts. And Annapolis will be climate ready. Its infrastructure will be designed to withstand or adapt to the impacts from climate change. The city will protect its communities and institutions most at risk of climate impacts; and the city will reduce its carbon emissions through a variety of coordinated policies, programs, and investments.

A multi-year investment strategy – a strategic set of revitalization initiatives and projects that local partners believe will increase the economic vitality and livability of their community, increase prosperity for local households and improve the health of the surrounding environment.

plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes the importance of, "Expanding opportunities for early childhood education programs and services in the county to ensure that all children have access to high quality early educational programs, which are predictors to success later in life."

plan_quotes.text: In Frederick County, 34,688 households, 39 percent, could not afford basic needs such as housing, child care, food, transportation, health care and technology in 2016.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 City of Frederick Comprehensive Plan cites a 2016 study indicating that for many households, basic needs are out of reach, noting that "39 percent, could not afford basic needs such as housing, child care, food, transportation, health care and technology."

plan_quotes.text: This Plan’s policies support a strong local economy with access to jobs, services and amenities, a healthier lifestyle by promoting and accommodating alternative transportation options, improved parks and recreational activities, as well as access to nutritious food choices.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 City of Frederick Comprehensive Plan highlights that its policies support a healthier lifestyle through initiatives that include providing "access to nutritious food choices."

plan_quotes.text: The City has also been able to increase food access by incorporating food trees into the tree canopy. In 2018, food forests were incorporated into the planting schedule in Baker and Waterford parks that are accessible by the Shared Use Path. This is in addition to 72 city-managed community garden plots available to residents for a small fee.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 City of Frederick Comprehensive Plan notes efforts to "increase food access by incorporating food trees into the tree canopy... in addition to 72 city-managed community garden plots available to residents for a small fee."

plan_quotes.text: Support local farms and farmers to grow produce for local use, resulting in a reduction in greenhouse gases from transportation and fresher healthy options for our people.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key policy in the 2021 City of Frederick Comprehensive Plan is to "Support local farms and farmers to grow produce for local use, resulting in... fresher healthy options for our people."

plan_quotes.text: Several communities mention a dearth of grocery stores.

plan_quotes.text: Liberty Road is a food desert, there are so few locations to acquire fresh food and produce, with such close farmland, the County needs to find ways to get the fresh produce being grown locally sold locally. Perhaps a cooperative?

plan_quotes.text: Affordable child care vs Pre-K/ Alternatives (funding for one parent to stay home. Affordable Meeting space facilities (Libraries))

plan_quotes.text: Reduce the number of food deserts and promote access to healthy food for all ages, particularly in low/moderate income communities.

plan_quotes.text: Bring in facilities like day cares, decent shopping center, better grocery stores, good schools and parks to attract young families.

plan_quotes.text: Explore options of higher end grocery stores and cafes similar to Catonsville and Ellicott City.

plan_quotes.text: Work with partners including the UMBC, Guinness Brewery, GABA Baltimore County Arts Guild to create and support more outdoor events, health and wellness facility, dog park, farmer’s market, community center, arts and events to cater UMBC students, murals, tourists and bring more amenities to the area.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 Arbutus Sustainable Community Application highlights a strategy to enhance community life and work with partners to create amenities such as a "farmer’s market, community center, arts and events to cater UMBC students, murals, tourists and bring more amenities to the area."

plan_areas.community_vision: Thrive Montgomery 2050 aims to create communities that offer equitable access to jobs, more housing, transportation, parks, and public spaces. Just as importantly, it can help guide the design of the built environment to strengthen the social and physical health of our residents, supporting active lifestyles and encouraging interaction and engagement.

Thrive Montgomery 2050 strives to create racially integrated and just communities by advancing just planning policies and public investments in underserved communities, promoting the racial and economic integration of neighborhoods, and focusing on the potential for the design of communities to help build social trust and inclusion while encouraging civic participation.

plan_quotes.text: As the county plans for the future, it should continue to find ways to address the specific needs of the vulnerable populations impacted by the hidden costs of poverty and determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan observes the need to "determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation."

plan_quotes.text: Improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan highlights the need to "improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism."

plan_quotes.text: Likewise, community gardens help to reduce the impact of food deserts in low-income areas, encourage physical activity and social interaction, and give residents who do not have yards access to nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy lifestyle.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan notes that, "community gardens help to reduce the impact of food deserts in low-income areas... and give residents who do not have yards access to nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy lifestyle."

plan_quotes.text: Continue DEP’s efforts to reduce wasted food and development of recommendations for a County-wide edible food recovery program. Provide focused education and outreach campaign “Food Is Too Good to Waste” to encourage and motivate residents and businesses to reduce wasted food, conduct focused education to shoppers providing tips to reduce wasted food, and continue research and survey assistance to measure the amount of edible food available for recovery from commercial food establishments.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Montgomery County Sustainable Communities Renewal application outlines a strategy to 'continue research and survey assistance to measure the amount of edible food available for recovery from commercial food establishments.'

plan_quotes.text: Relieve financial stress on farmers and encourage start-up agritourism businesses in/around the County’s 93K-acre Ag Reserve to help increase farm-related profitability, generate additional tourism spending and increase the County’s tax revenue while developing tourism products in the County’s rural areas that are open, accessible and identifiable to the County’s diverse residents and visitors.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key economic goal in the 2023 Montgomery County Sustainable Communities Renewal application is to 'relieve financial stress on farmers and encourage start-up agritourism businesses in/around the County’s 93K-acre Ag Reserve.'

plan_areas.community_vision: Through numerous public meetings, research and data collection and discussions with people who have worked diligently to improve Allegany County, a picture of this area has more clearly come into focus; the key theme of this portrait centers upon improved vitality, economic health and enhanced livability. This picture includes removal of blight and supporting infill development, economic development concentrated in or around existing municipalities, eco-tourism resulting from new trail extensions and connectivity, preservation of sensitive and critical areas, investment and citizen pride in Allegany County.
Cumberland’s focus on providing a great place to live and a supportive place to build a profitable business to be realized through a comprehensive approach.

plan_quotes.text: Availability of quality childcare is an important factor in the County’s economy and quality of life. According to Maryland Child Care Network-Child Care Demographics 2012, the following data for Allegany County was reported: Family Child Care Providers: 73 with a capacity for 550 children. Child Care Centers (8-12 hours): 17 with a capacity for 1,037 children.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2014 Allegany County Comprehensive Plan highlights that, "Availability of quality childcare is an important factor in the County’s economy and quality of life." The plan references 2012 data indicating the county had 73 Family Child Care Providers with a capacity for 550 children and 17 Child Care Centers with a capacity for 1,037 children.

plan_quotes.text: Develop strategy to provide quality childcare for children between the ages of 0 and 12 at a cost not to exceed 10% of household income.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key recommendation in the 2014 Allegany County Comprehensive Plan is to, "Develop strategy to provide quality childcare for children between the ages of 0 and 12 at a cost not to exceed 10% of household income."

plan_areas.community_vision: PlanQAC’s vision is to preserve the County as a quintessential rural community whose overall character exemplifies it as: A GREAT PLACE TO LIVE—Queen Anne’s County is a predominantly rural county with small towns connected by creeks and county roads through fields and forests; A GOOD PLACE TO WORK—Queen Anne’s County encourages agriculture, seafood and maritime industries, tourism and outdoor sports, and small business and high-tech enterprise; A GOOD NEIGHBOR—Queen Anne’s County is a faithful steward of its natural and cultural heritage for the Chesapeake Bay and other Eastern Shore counties; A PROTECTIVE COMMUNITY—Queen Anne’s County cultivates its citizens’ expectations and opportunities, emphasizing that development should not impair the quality of life enjoyed by all; A SUPPORTIVE COUNTY—Queen Anne’s County supports the highest quality of education for its citizens, seeking to fully prepare them for the future.

plan_areas.community_vision: Our ultimate goal is to maintain and enhance Harford County’s quality of life. HarfordNEXT represents a bold and imaginative vision that will make our community stronger and prosperous for generations.

In the coming years, Annapolis will be a more equitable, healthy, and resilient city. It will be a more walkable and connected city where multiple safe and reliable transportation options reduce personal vehicle dependency. It will be a city which prioritizes public investments in its most socially vulnerable communities; a city which expands housing options accessible to residents of all income levels; and a city which grows a community of diverse local entrepreneurs aided by inclusive economic programs and opportunities. Annapolis will be a city which prioritizes the preservation, restoration, maintenance, and enhancement of its natural resources, particularly when planning for new development. It will be a city which ensures that all residents have access to high quality recreational amenities particularly public water access; and it will be a city which values its cultural life through support for arts initiatives, artists and arts organizations, and citywide historic preservation efforts. And Annapolis will be climate ready. Its infrastructure will be designed to withstand or adapt to the impacts from climate change. The city will protect its communities and institutions most at risk of climate impacts; and the city will reduce its carbon emissions through a variety of coordinated policies, programs, and investments.

A multi-year investment strategy – a strategic set of revitalization initiatives and projects that local partners believe will increase the economic vitality and livability of their community, increase prosperity for local households and improve the health of the surrounding environment.

plan_quotes.text: One area of the city classified as a food desert by the USDA according to 2019 data is the Eastport neighborhood between Tyler Avenue/Hilltop Lane and Adams Street to the west of Bay Ridge Avenue, where there is a high rate of poverty for the region, low vehicle access, and poor proximity to supermarkets.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Annapolis Ahead Comprehensive Plan 2040 identifies that, "One area of the city classified as a food desert by the USDA...is the Eastport neighborhood...where there is a high rate of poverty for the region, low vehicle access, and poor proximity to supermarkets."

plan_quotes.text: A small grocery should be included in future redevelopment to address a well-documented gap in food access.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Annapolis Ahead Comprehensive Plan 2040 notes the need for a grocery store in Eastport, stating that, "A small grocery should be included in future redevelopment to address a well-documented gap in food access."

plan_quotes.text: Efforts should be made to broaden the reach of the farmers’ markets to communities with a documented need for improved access to healthy food.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Annapolis Ahead Comprehensive Plan 2040 recommends that, "Efforts should be made to broaden the reach of the farmers’ markets to communities with a documented need for improved access to healthy food."

plan_quotes.text: The City is also looking to address access to healthy foods and eliminate an existing food desert within the Sustainable Community area. Land use limitations have proven to be a challenge to this effort but a new focus on creating a food cooperative that would require a smaller development footprint than a conventional grocery is gaining momentum.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 City of Annapolis Sustainable Communities Renewal Application notes the city is looking to "address access to healthy foods and eliminate an existing food desert within the Sustainable Community area," with a new focus on creating a food cooperative.

plan_quotes.text: Similar to the previous Sustainable Communities renewal, food deserts are still a concentrated issue within Annapolis that have yet to be eliminated within a portion of the city.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 City of Annapolis Sustainable Communities Renewal Application highlights an ongoing need, stating that "food deserts are still a concentrated issue within Annapolis that have yet to be eliminated within a portion of the city."

plan_quotes.text: Well-documented food desert
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key challenge identified in the 2024 City of Annapolis Sustainable Communities Renewal Application is the presence of a "Well-documented food desert."

plan_quotes.text: Coordinate retail strategy as part of the Eastport CNI project to ensure a small grocery or other healthy food provider is part of the redevelopment.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: To address food deserts, the 2024 City of Annapolis Sustainable Communities Renewal Application proposes a strategy to "ensure a small grocery or other healthy food provider is part of the redevelopment" of the Eastport community.

plan_areas.community_vision: Our ultimate goal is to maintain and enhance Harford County’s quality of life. HarfordNEXT represents a bold and imaginative vision that will make our community stronger and prosperous for generations.

Support and maintain a desired quality of life encouraging economic prosperity and cultural enjoyment that focuses on retaining and expanding the Town role as an economic, cultural, governmental, medical and social center fostering big city vibrancy while retaining small town charm.

The Sustainable Communities Action Plan update is based on the 2022 Comprehensive Plan for the Town of Bel Air. Goals and objectives regarding sustainable practices are interwoven throughout the entire source document and these elements served as the basis for the Sustainable Communities Action Plan and were included as measurable actions, policies, and programs.

plan_quotes.text: Improve early childhood education programs and provide assistance to parents in order to ensure their children are ready for school.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2016 HarfordNEXT plan highlights the need to "Improve early childhood education programs and provide assistance to parents in order to ensure their children are ready for school."

plan_quotes.text: 9% Food Insecurity. 3% Lack of Access to Healthy Food.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2016 HarfordNEXT plan identifies that within the county, "There is a 9% food insecurity rate and 3% of the population lacks access to healthy food."

plan_quotes.text: Quality locally sourced food should be available to all residents. Farm-to-table programs benefit farmers through increased revenue, and residents benefit from healthy, locally sourced fresh produce.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key goal in the 2016 HarfordNEXT plan is ensuring that "Quality locally sourced food should be available to all residents."

plan_quotes.text: Community gardens and urban farms increase the availability of fresh fruits and vegetables and provide awareness of the environment and the science of cultivation, and incorporating it as a way of life.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2016 HarfordNEXT plan highlights that "Community gardens and urban farms increase the availability of fresh fruits and vegetables and provide awareness of the environment."

plan_quotes.text: Support farmers markets that allow for electronic benefit transfer (EBT) so that vulnerable populations can have access to healthy locally grown foods.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: To improve food access for all, the 2016 HarfordNEXT plan recommends to "Support farmers markets that allow for electronic benefit transfer (EBT) so that vulnerable populations can have access to healthy locally grown foods."

plan_quotes.text: Identify areas in the County that lack access to healthy foods or supermarkets.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2016 HarfordNEXT plan calls to "Identify areas in the County that lack access to healthy foods or supermarkets."

plan_quotes.text: The greatest potential is for full-service restaurants with data indicating the potential to support up to 20 new restaurants and additional demand for clothing stores and specialty grocery and food services.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Town of Bel Air Comprehensive Plan's market analysis indicates "additional demand for clothing stores and specialty grocery and food services."

plan_quotes.text: The Mall owners sold a portion of the site containing the former Sears store. The developers are proposing to tear down the vacant Sears space and build a high-end grocery store with additional retail.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Town of Bel Air Comprehensive Plan notes a significant redevelopment proposal where developers are planning to "build a high-end grocery store with additional retail."

plan_quotes.text: The Town provides opportunity for residents and visitors to enjoy local food and agricultural products through the Bel Air Farmers Market. This market has thrived for over forty-five years in the downtown area supporting the need for organic foods, local farm harvest and value-added products that cannot be obtained elsewhere in the region.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Town of Bel Air Comprehensive Plan highlights a key community asset, noting that the Bel Air Farmers Market has "thrived for over forty-five years in the downtown area supporting the need for organic foods, local farm harvest and value-added products that cannot be obtained elsewhere in the region."

In the coming years, Annapolis will be a more equitable, healthy, and resilient city. It will be a more walkable and connected city where multiple safe and reliable transportation options reduce personal vehicle dependency. It will be a city which prioritizes public investments in its most socially vulnerable communities; a city which expands housing options accessible to residents of all income levels; and a city which grows a community of diverse local entrepreneurs aided by inclusive economic programs and opportunities. Annapolis will be a city which prioritizes the preservation, restoration, maintenance, and enhancement of its natural resources, particularly when planning for new development. It will be a city which ensures that all residents have access to high quality recreational amenities particularly public water access; and it will be a city which values its cultural life through support for arts initiatives, artists and arts organizations, and citywide historic preservation efforts. And Annapolis will be climate ready. Its infrastructure will be designed to withstand or adapt to the impacts from climate change. The city will protect its communities and institutions most at risk of climate impacts; and the city will reduce its carbon emissions through a variety of coordinated policies, programs, and investments.

A multi-year investment strategy – a strategic set of revitalization initiatives and projects that local partners believe will increase the economic vitality and livability of their community, increase prosperity for local households and improve the health of the surrounding environment.

plan_quotes.text: One area of the city classified as a food desert by the USDA according to 2019 data is the Eastport neighborhood between Tyler Avenue/Hilltop Lane and Adams Street to the west of Bay Ridge Avenue, where there is a high rate of poverty for the region, low vehicle access, and poor proximity to supermarkets.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Annapolis Ahead Comprehensive Plan 2040 identifies that, "One area of the city classified as a food desert by the USDA...is the Eastport neighborhood...where there is a high rate of poverty for the region, low vehicle access, and poor proximity to supermarkets."

plan_quotes.text: A small grocery should be included in future redevelopment to address a well-documented gap in food access.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Annapolis Ahead Comprehensive Plan 2040 notes the need for a grocery store in Eastport, stating that, "A small grocery should be included in future redevelopment to address a well-documented gap in food access."

plan_quotes.text: Efforts should be made to broaden the reach of the farmers’ markets to communities with a documented need for improved access to healthy food.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Annapolis Ahead Comprehensive Plan 2040 recommends that, "Efforts should be made to broaden the reach of the farmers’ markets to communities with a documented need for improved access to healthy food."

plan_quotes.text: The City is also looking to address access to healthy foods and eliminate an existing food desert within the Sustainable Community area. plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 City of Annapolis Sustainable Communities Renewal Application notes the city is looking to "address access to healthy foods and eliminate an existing food desert within the Sustainable Community area," with a new focus on creating a food cooperative.

plan_quotes.text: Similar to the previous Sustainable Communities renewal, food deserts are still a concentrated issue within Annapolis that have yet to be eliminated within a portion of the city.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 City of Annapolis Sustainable Communities Renewal Application highlights an ongoing need, stating that "food deserts are still a concentrated issue within Annapolis that have yet to be eliminated within a portion of the city."

In the coming years, Annapolis will be a more equitable, healthy, and resilient city. It will be a more walkable and connected city where multiple safe and reliable transportation options reduce personal vehicle dependency. It will be a city which prioritizes public investments in its most socially vulnerable communities; a city which expands housing options accessible to residents of all income levels; and a city which grows a community of diverse local entrepreneurs aided by inclusive economic programs and opportunities. Annapolis will be a city which prioritizes the preservation, restoration, maintenance, and enhancement of its natural resources, particularly when planning for new development. It will be a city which ensures that all residents have access to high quality recreational amenities particularly public water access; and it will be a city which values its cultural life through support for arts initiatives, artists and arts organizations, and citywide historic preservation efforts. And Annapolis will be climate ready. Its infrastructure will be designed to withstand or adapt to the impacts from climate change. The city will protect its communities and institutions most at risk of climate impacts; and the city will reduce its carbon emissions through a variety of coordinated policies, programs, and investments.

plan_quotes.text: Improve early childhood education programs and provide assistance to parents in order to ensure their children are ready for school.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2016 HarfordNEXT plan highlights the need to "Improve early childhood education programs and provide assistance to parents in order to ensure their children are ready for school."

plan_quotes.text: 9% Food Insecurity. 3% Lack of Access to Healthy Food.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2016 HarfordNEXT plan identifies that within the county, "There is a 9% food insecurity rate and 3% of the population lacks access to healthy food."

plan_quotes.text: Quality locally sourced food should be available to all residents. Farm-to-table programs benefit farmers through increased revenue, and residents benefit from healthy, locally sourced fresh produce.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key goal in the 2016 HarfordNEXT plan is ensuring that "Quality locally sourced food should be available to all residents."

plan_quotes.text: Community gardens and urban farms increase the availability of fresh fruits and vegetables and provide awareness of the environment and the science of cultivation, and incorporating it as a way of life.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2016 HarfordNEXT plan highlights that "Community gardens and urban farms increase the availability of fresh fruits and vegetables and provide awareness of the environment."

plan_quotes.text: Support farmers markets that allow for electronic benefit transfer (EBT) so that vulnerable populations can have access to healthy locally grown foods.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: To improve food access for all, the 2016 HarfordNEXT plan recommends to "Support farmers markets that allow for electronic benefit transfer (EBT) so that vulnerable populations can have access to healthy locally grown foods."

plan_quotes.text: Identify areas in the County that lack access to healthy foods or supermarkets.

plan_quotes.text: The Green Team has four community gardens in which over 50 households grow food. Volunteers at the Heirloom Victory Garden grow produce that is donated to three local food pantries.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 City of Havre de Grace Sustainable Communities Plan highlights community-led food initiatives, noting that volunteers at the Heirloom Victory Garden "grow produce that is donated to three local food pantries."

plan_quotes.text: Havre de Grace has hosted a local farmers market for over ten years. It has continued to grow and is now a managed under a non-profit organization by a group of over 35 farmers and local vendors.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key community asset identified in the 2022 City of Havre de Grace Sustainable Communities Plan is that the city "has hosted a local farmers market for over ten years."

plan_quotes.text: St. Johns Episcopalian Church kitchen/pantry provides weekly hot meals to people in need, each Friday year round, averaging between 100-150 meals per week.

plan_quotes.text: Chapter 205 – Zoning – Multiple ordinances have been written by the Department of Planning and adopted by City Council to address issues such as historic streetscape preservation, ease parking requirements for existing lots in the downtown, and add permitted and conditional uses such as daycare and assisted living facilities.

plan_quotes.text: The new high school offers both college preparatory education and vocational training programs for students interested in careers in preschool education or restaurants/food service industry with access to a functioning greenhouse.

plan_areas.community_vision: Preserve and enhance the quality of life, by recognizing and protecting the unique character of St. Mary's County as a Chesapeake Bay peninsula. Foster economic growth and create an atmosphere of excellence by focusing and managing growth to create vibrant, attractive communities; by protecting the rural character and economy of the countryside by nurturing the shoreline and adjacent waters; and by preserving and capitalizing on the natural resources and historical quality of the County.

The overall vision for the Comprehensive Plan is to maintain the historical character while embracing growth that is occurring in and around the Town’s municipal boundary. Key elements of this vision include: a vital and thriving downtown; a sustained appreciation and commitment to the protection of the town’s historic resources; broader public access to waterfront resources and enhancing the sense of identity as a “waterfront” community; provision of a wide range of services and events that support and enrich the quality of life for both Town and County residents; and management of anticipated growth to shape its form, scale, and qualities to protect and preserve the “small town” character.

Leonardtown is fast becoming a family-friendly, independent business, and restaurant hub in St. Mary's County, and offers a distinct sense of place centered amidst an array of water, nature and cultural-based amenities.

plan_quotes.text: Community gardens and urban farms increase the availability of fresh fruits and vegetables and provide awareness of the environment and the science of cultivation, and incorporating it as a way of life.

plan_quotes.text: The Green Team has four community gardens in which over 50 households grow food. Volunteers at the Heirloom Victory Garden grow produce that is donated to three local food pantries.

plan_quotes.text: Havre de Grace has hosted a local farmers market for over ten years. It has continued to grow and is now a managed under a non-profit organization by a group of over 35 farmers and local vendors.

plan_quotes.text: St. Johns Episcopalian Church kitchen/pantry provides weekly hot meals to people in need, each Friday year round, averaging between 100-150 meals per week.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 City of Havre de Grace Sustainable Communities Plan recognizes vital local support systems, noting that a church pantry "provides weekly hot meals to people in need, each Friday year round, averaging between 100-150 meals per week."

plan_quotes.text: Chapter 205 – Zoning – Multiple ordinances have been written by the Department of Planning and adopted by City Council to address issues such as historic streetscape preservation, ease parking requirements for existing lots in the downtown, and add permitted and conditional uses such as daycare and assisted living facilities.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 City of Havre de Grace Sustainable Communities Plan notes that local zoning ordinances have been updated to "add permitted and conditional uses such as daycare and assisted living facilities."

plan_quotes.text: The new high school offers both college preparatory education and vocational training programs for students interested in careers in preschool education or restaurants/food service industry with access to a functioning greenhouse.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 City of Havre de Grace Sustainable Communities Plan notes that the new high school provides opportunities for residents by offering "vocational training programs for students interested in careers in preschool education."

plan_areas.community_vision: Thrive Montgomery 2050 aims to create communities that offer equitable access to jobs, more housing, transportation, parks, and public spaces. Just as importantly, it can help guide the design of the built environment to strengthen the social and physical health of our residents, supporting active lifestyles and encouraging interaction and engagement.

Thrive Montgomery 2050 strives to create racially integrated and just communities by advancing just planning policies and public investments in underserved communities, promoting the racial and economic integration of neighborhoods, and focusing on the potential for the design of communities to help build social trust and inclusion while encouraging civic participation.

plan_quotes.text: As the county plans for the future, it should continue to find ways to address the specific needs of the vulnerable populations impacted by the hidden costs of poverty and determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan observes the need to "determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation."

plan_quotes.text: Improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan highlights the need to "improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism."

plan_quotes.text: Likewise, community gardens help to reduce the impact of food deserts in low-income areas, encourage physical activity and social interaction, and give residents who do not have yards access to nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy lifestyle.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan notes that, "community gardens help to reduce the impact of food deserts in low-income areas... and give residents who do not have yards access to nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy lifestyle."

plan_quotes.text: Continue DEP’s efforts to reduce wasted food and development of recommendations for a County-wide edible food recovery program. Provide focused education and outreach campaign “Food Is Too Good to Waste” to encourage and motivate residents and businesses to reduce wasted food, conduct focused education to shoppers providing tips to reduce wasted food, and continue research and survey assistance to measure the amount of edible food available for recovery from commercial food establishments.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Montgomery County Sustainable Communities Renewal application outlines a strategy to 'continue research and survey assistance to measure the amount of edible food available for recovery from commercial food establishments.'

plan_quotes.text: Relieve financial stress on farmers and encourage start-up agritourism businesses in/around the County’s 93K-acre Ag Reserve to help increase farm-related profitability, generate additional tourism spending and increase the County’s tax revenue while developing tourism products in the County’s rural areas that are open, accessible and identifiable to the County’s diverse residents and visitors.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key economic goal in the 2023 Montgomery County Sustainable Communities Renewal application is to 'relieve financial stress on farmers and encourage start-up agritourism businesses in/around the County’s 93K-acre Ag Reserve.'

plan_quotes.text: Several communities mention a dearth of grocery stores.

plan_areas.community_vision: In 2035, Prince George’s County is the community of choice for families, businesses, and workers in the region. It is distinguished by strong, green, and healthy communities; a competitive, innovative, and adaptive economy; vibrant and walkable mixed-use centers; quality open space; restored ecosystems; and iconic destinations. It meets the diverse needs of all Prince Georgians and embraces and builds on the momentum generated by new residents, technology, and business opportunities.

plan_areas.community_vision: By embracing its rich Chesapeake culture and heritage, invaluable ecosystems and emerging opportunities, Anne Arundel County embodies the best of both the past and future, providing its residents a place where all are proud to live, work, learn, and play.

In the coming years, Annapolis will be a more equitable, healthy, and resilient city. It will be a more walkable and connected city where multiple safe and reliable transportation options reduce personal vehicle dependency. It will be a city which prioritizes public investments in its most socially vulnerable communities; a city which expands housing options accessible to residents of all income levels; and a city which grows a community of diverse local entrepreneurs aided by inclusive economic programs and opportunities. Annapolis will be a city which prioritizes the preservation, restoration, maintenance, and enhancement of its natural resources, particularly when planning for new development. It will be a city which ensures that all residents have access to high quality recreational amenities particularly public water access; and it will be a city which values its cultural life through support for arts initiatives, artists and arts organizations, and citywide historic preservation efforts. And Annapolis will be climate ready. Its infrastructure will be designed to withstand or adapt to the impacts from climate change. The city will protect its communities and institutions most at risk of climate impacts; and the city will reduce its carbon emissions through a variety of coordinated policies, programs, and investments.

A multi-year investment strategy – a strategic set of revitalization initiatives and projects that local partners believe will increase the economic vitality and livability of their community, increase prosperity for local households and improve the health of the surrounding environment.

plan_quotes.text: Much of North County is a food desert, with few locations where healthy food can be purchased.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 Plan2040 for Anne Arundel County notes that, "Much of North County is a food desert, with few locations where healthy food can be purchased."

plan_quotes.text: Approximately 75,000 (13.2%) County residents live in an area categorized as a food desert, which is an urban neighborhood or rural town without ready access to fresh, healthy and affordable food.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 Plan2040 for Anne Arundel County highlights a significant statistic that, "Approximately 75,000 (13.2%) County residents live in an area categorized as a food desert, which is an urban neighborhood or rural town without ready access to fresh, healthy and affordable food."

plan_quotes.text: Work with local employers to provide job training and readiness programs as well as support services such as childcare and transportation to ensure residents can take advantage of employment opportunities in the County.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 Plan2040 for Anne Arundel County identifies a strategy to, "Work with local employers to provide job training and readiness programs as well as support services such as childcare and transportation to ensure residents can take advantage of employment opportunities in the County."

plan_quotes.text: One area of the city classified as a food desert by the USDA according to 2019 data is the Eastport neighborhood between Tyler Avenue/Hilltop Lane and Adams Street to the west of Bay Ridge Avenue, where there is a high rate of poverty for the region, low vehicle access, and poor proximity to supermarkets.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Annapolis Ahead Comprehensive Plan 2040 identifies that, "One area of the city classified as a food desert by the USDA...is the Eastport neighborhood...where there is a high rate of poverty for the region, low vehicle access, and poor proximity to supermarkets."

plan_quotes.text: A small grocery should be included in future redevelopment to address a well-documented gap in food access.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Annapolis Ahead Comprehensive Plan 2040 notes the need for a grocery store in Eastport, stating that, "A small grocery should be included in future redevelopment to address a well-documented gap in food access."

plan_quotes.text: Efforts should be made to broaden the reach of the farmers’ markets to communities with a documented need for improved access to healthy food.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Annapolis Ahead Comprehensive Plan 2040 recommends that, "Efforts should be made to broaden the reach of the farmers’ markets to communities with a documented need for improved access to healthy food."

plan_quotes.text: The City is also looking to address access to healthy foods and eliminate an existing food desert within the Sustainable Community area. Land use limitations have proven to be a challenge to this effort but a new focus on creating a food cooperative that would require a smaller development footprint than a conventional grocery is gaining momentum.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 City of Annapolis Sustainable Communities Renewal Application notes the city is looking to "address access to healthy foods and eliminate an existing food desert within the Sustainable Community area," with a new focus on creating a food cooperative.

plan_quotes.text: Similar to the previous Sustainable Communities renewal, food deserts are still a concentrated issue within Annapolis that have yet to be eliminated within a portion of the city.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 City of Annapolis Sustainable Communities Renewal Application highlights an ongoing need, stating that "food deserts are still a concentrated issue within Annapolis that have yet to be eliminated within a portion of the city."

plan_quotes.text: Well-documented food desert
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key challenge identified in the 2024 City of Annapolis Sustainable Communities Renewal Application is the presence of a "Well-documented food desert."

plan_quotes.text: Coordinate retail strategy as part of the Eastport CNI project to ensure a small grocery or other healthy food provider is part of the redevelopment.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: To address food deserts, the 2024 City of Annapolis Sustainable Communities Renewal Application proposes a strategy to "ensure a small grocery or other healthy food provider is part of the redevelopment" of the Eastport community.
