The Town of Sykesville offers an exceptional quality of life for all residents by enhancing the Downtown as a high-quality, small-town center; preserving its unique history; connecting neighborhoods, parks, and Downtown with an accessible network of trails and sidewalks; protecting the natural environment; and continuing to deliver high-quality public services.

The Vision 2030 comprehensive plan serves as the official policy guide for short term and long-term decision making relative to priority investments in the town of Sykesville, focusing on Main Street revitalization, park expansion, and economic development.

plan_quotes.text: In a community survey asking 'What kinds of businesses would you like to see more of in the downtown?', 51% of respondents found a 'Grocery/health food store' to be 'Very Desirable' and 42% found it 'Somewhat Desirable'.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 Sykesville Comprehensive Plan includes survey results indicating a strong community interest in new food options, noting that for a "Grocery/health food store," 51% of respondents found it 'Very Desirable' and 42% found it 'Somewhat Desirable'.

plan_quotes.text: In addition to public schools within the Carroll County Public School System, the Town of Sykesville is served by the Immanuel and Ava Wanas Montessori School, located at 7590 College Road. The school specializes in kindergarten and infant care by actively facilitating a learning environment that nurtures children's innate ability to learn both emotionally and academically at an early age.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 Sykesville Comprehensive Plan notes the presence of local educational facilities, including a Montessori School that "specializes in kindergarten and infant care by actively facilitating a learning environment that nurtures children's innate ability to learn."

plan_quotes.text: There are a variety of grocery stores within a reasonable distance to the sustainable community as well as a farmers’ market on Main Street with many different options including fresh meat and produce during part of the year.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 Vision 2030 comprehensive plan notes that, "There are a variety of grocery stores within a reasonable distance to the sustainable community as well as a farmers’ market on Main Street with many different options including fresh meat and produce during part of the year."

plan_quotes.text: There is a community produce garden that is maintained on the lawn of the Town House where citizens are encouraged to volunteer and harvest their own produce.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: As part of its community health initiatives, the 2021 Vision 2030 comprehensive plan highlights a, "Community produce garden that is maintained on the lawn of the Town House where citizens are encouraged to volunteer and harvest their own produce."

plan_quotes.text: The City has several grocery stores that offer fresh food and organic food options. The City also sponsors a Farmer’s Market that is held weekly from May to November that promotes local farmers’ products and produce. This year, the City’s Farmer’s Market will also operate several weekends throughout the Winter. The City provides space for a community garden (Key Street) where residents are encouraged to maintain their own garden on a specific plot. The City provides 15 plots.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 City of Westminster Sustainable Communities Renewal Application notes that, "The City also sponsors a Farmer’s Market that is held weekly from May to November... The City provides space for a community garden (Key Street) where residents are encouraged to maintain their own garden on a specific plot."

plan_quotes.text: The Boys and Girls Club of America opened a new facility in downtown which adds numerous programs, summer camps and a daycare for disadvantaged youth.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 City of Westminster Sustainable Communities Renewal Application highlights the addition of a key community resource, noting that, "The Boys and Girls Club of America opened a new facility in downtown which adds numerous programs, summer camps and a daycare for disadvantaged youth."

plan_areas.community_vision: Rockville will be a vibrant, multicultural, and socio-economically inclusive city with distinct neighborhoods that are supported by a strong local economy, a healthy natural environment, and a desirable quality of life founded on a responsive government.

Thrive Montgomery 2050 aims to create communities that offer equitable access to jobs, more housing, transportation, parks, and public spaces. Just as importantly, it can help guide the design of the built environment to strengthen the social and physical health of our residents, supporting active lifestyles and encouraging interaction and engagement.

plan_quotes.text: Rockville is generally well served by a range of full-service supermarkets and specialty food stores. However residents without access to a car may face challenges, particularly those residents with lower incomes.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 City of Rockville Comprehensive Plan observes that while the city is generally well-served by supermarkets, "residents without access to a car may face challenges, particularly those residents with lower incomes."

plan_quotes.text: Seek opportunities for fresh food and other goods and services for residents of David Scull Courts and other nearby residents and workers.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 City of Rockville Comprehensive Plan identifies a need to "Seek opportunities for fresh food and other goods and services for residents of David Scull Courts and other nearby residents and workers."

plan_quotes.text: Residents have indicated concerns about potential adverse impacts of traffic, excessive on-street parking, and noise; and believe that the number and size of child care centers should be limited to preserve the residential character of the neighborhood.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 City of Rockville Comprehensive Plan highlights the community's desire to balance the need for child care with preserving neighborhood character, noting concerns about potential impacts from "traffic, excessive on-street parking, and noise."

plan_quotes.text: Cultivate a local food system that provides residents of all income levels access to healthy fresh food and improves food security.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key goal of the 2021 City of Rockville Comprehensive Plan is to "Cultivate a local food system that provides residents of all income levels access to healthy fresh food and improves food security."

plan_quotes.text: As the county plans for the future, it should continue to find ways to address the specific needs of the vulnerable populations impacted by the hidden costs of poverty and determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan observes the need to "determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation."

plan_quotes.text: Improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan highlights the need to "improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism."

plan_quotes.text: Likewise, community gardens help to reduce the impact of food deserts in low-income areas, encourage physical activity and social interaction, and give residents who do not have yards access to nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy lifestyle.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan notes that, "community gardens help to reduce the impact of food deserts in low-income areas... and give residents who do not have yards access to nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy lifestyle."

plan_quotes.text: Agriculture is vibrant and viable. People love fresh food and farm to fork.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key community value identified in the 2019 Livable Frederick Master Plan is that, "Agriculture is vibrant and viable. People love fresh food and farm to fork."

plan_quotes.text: Promote the development of community gardens within new and existing communities to increase access to fresh and nutritious food choices.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2019 Livable Frederick Master Plan encourages planners to, "Promote the development of community gardens within new and existing communities to increase access to fresh and nutritious food choices."

plan_quotes.text: Eliminate food deserts in the county by pursuing strategies to provide more widespread availability and affordability of fresh and healthy food choices.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights the goal to, "Eliminate food deserts in the county by pursuing strategies to provide more widespread availability and affordability of fresh and healthy food choices."

plan_quotes.text: Support mobile markets and fresh food carts or vehicles that travel to neighborhoods on a set schedule to sell fresh fruits and vegetables and that accept a variety of payment methods.

In 2040, Thurmont is a vibrant community with an active downtown where both new and historic buildings are occupied with successful businesses and residents. The Town’s abundant park system is interconnected with new open spaces and trails, and an abundant number of trees are planted throughout the Town. Thurmont has succeeded at encouraging new businesses and clean industry, embraced technological advances in telecommunications, and promoted walking, biking, outdoor recreation, and community wide celebrations.

plan_areas.community_vision: Howard County is a welcoming and inclusive community that residents are proud to call home. Our collective vision is to accommodate future growth in a manner that retains and improves upon the unique and diverse community character of Howard County. We will continue to support, promote, and act toward creating a community grounded in civility, sustainable development patterns, environmental stewardship, and well-maintained supporting infrastructure. Policies and investments will respect and prioritize the natural environment, historic resources and agricultural heritage, diverse cultures and people, and established community character in an equitable, predictable, sustainable, and achievable way for generations to come.
The goal of creating 'A Vibrant Village Center For Today' is being met through implementing a stabilization plan of maintenance, repair, beautification and placemaking.

plan_quotes.text: Some participants advocated for more food options located closer to carless households. Columbia’s walkable village centers were identified as good locations for restaurants and grocery stores featuring locally-sourced food.

plan_quotes.text: Sustainability and food security mean preservation of our local farms and pollinators.

plan_quotes.text: To ensure underserved populations can participate in training, entities involved in workforce development should partner to offer resources such as child care.

plan_quotes.text: Access to local foods has been improving but still is limited in the Village Center, with Roving Radish being the main entity. plan_quotes.text: Five grocery stores are within a six-minute drive of the LRVC.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Long Reach Sustainable Community plan observes the local food landscape, noting that 'Five grocery stores are within a six-minute drive of the LRVC,' which provides context for village center retail planning.

plan_quotes.text: In 2020, Roving Radish, an award-winning Howard County program that provides healthy meal kits sourced from local farms, opened its first storefront in Long Reach Village Center. The 4,142 square foot space provides a storefront offering fresh meat, dairy, eggs, and milk from local and regional farms and serve as a kitchen, storage and packing space for the weekly meal kits.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Long Reach Sustainable Community plan highlights a key addition to the community, noting that, 'Roving Radish, an award-winning Howard County program that provides healthy meal kits sourced from local farms, opened its first storefront in Long Reach Village Center.'

plan_quotes.text: In 2020, Howard International Grocer, a market specializing in international foods and halal meat, moved into 1,733 square feet of the Long Reach Village Center, as part of the Long Reach Rising revitalization project led by Howard County. Howard International Grocer sells fresh and frozen meat and fish, fresh vegetables, fruit, milk, eggs, snacks, and more.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Long Reach Sustainable Community plan notes progress in food retail diversity, stating, 'Howard International Grocer, a market specializing in international foods and halal meat, moved into...the Long Reach Village Center...[and] sells fresh and frozen meat and fish, fresh vegetables, fruit, milk, eggs, snacks, and more.'

plan_quotes.text: Head Start, a vital early education program of the Community Action Council of Howard County, moved one of its locations to the Long Reach Village Center in 2020. The Long Reach location has approximately 5,332 square feet, allowing Head Start to increase its capacity from 38 to 80 children. Head Start provides free pre-school to eligible 3 to 5-year-old children.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Long Reach Sustainable Community plan highlights expanded access to early education, stating that a new Head Start location in the Village Center is 'allowing Head Start to increase its capacity from 38 to 80 children.'

plan_areas.community_vision: It is Kent County’s vision to preserve its historic and cultural traditions, along with its high quality of life, while embracing sufficient economic opportunities to provide for the economic well-being of our citizens. Agriculture is the linchpin that buttresses the County’s economy, culture, history, and everyday experiences. Kent County cannot afford to have this key element damaged or displaced. This recognition of agriculture’s status as the highest and best use for much of the County is an essential tenet of this Plan.

plan_areas.community_vision: Howard County is a welcoming and inclusive community that residents are proud to call home. Our collective vision is to accommodate future growth in a manner that retains and improves upon the unique and diverse community character of Howard County. We will continue to support, promote, and act toward creating a community grounded in civility, sustainable development patterns, environmental stewardship, and well-maintained supporting infrastructure. Policies and investments will respect and prioritize the natural environment, historic resources and agricultural heritage, diverse cultures and people, and established community character in an equitable, predictable, sustainable, and achievable way for generations to come.
North Laurel District is identified as a mixed use, walkable activity center in the recently adopted County’s general plan: HoCo By Design.

plan_quotes.text: Some participants advocated for more food options located closer to carless households. Columbia’s walkable village centers were identified as good locations for restaurants and grocery stores featuring locally-sourced food.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The HoCo By Design plan notes a community desire for "more food options located closer to carless households," identifying Columbia’s walkable village centers as good locations for restaurants and grocery stores featuring locally-sourced food.

plan_quotes.text: Use creative solutions to address food deserts (areas without healthy, fresh food options).
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key finding from community focus groups in the HoCo By Design plan is the need to "use creative solutions to address food deserts (areas without healthy, fresh food options)."

plan_quotes.text: Sustainability and food security mean preservation of our local farms and pollinators.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A resident's perspective in the HoCo By Design plan links environmental health to food systems, stating that, "Sustainability and food security mean preservation of our local farms and pollinators."

plan_quotes.text: To ensure underserved populations can participate in training, entities involved in workforce development should partner to offer resources such as child care.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The HoCo By Design plan highlights that to support economic opportunity, "entities involved in workforce development should partner to offer resources such as child care" to ensure underserved populations can participate in training.

plan_quotes.text: Lack of affordable daycare centers or early childhood education providers
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 North Laurel - Savage Sustainable Community Plan identifies a key community need, noting the "Lack of affordable daycare centers or early childhood education providers."

plan_quotes.text: Investigate locating a Head Start/Early Childhood education center to support eligible children and families in the North Laurel-Savage area.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 North Laurel - Savage Sustainable Community Plan proposes to "Investigate locating a Head Start/Early Childhood education center to support eligible children and families in the North Laurel-Savage area."

plan_quotes.text: The 2022 LPPRP supports continuing to locate a site for a community garden in North Laurel-Savage area which would alleviate the demand on other local community gardens and locate the resource closer to community members.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 North Laurel - Savage Sustainable Community Plan notes the ongoing need for local fresh food options, highlighting a goal to "locate a site for a community garden in the North Laurel-Savage area which would alleviate the demand on other local community gardens and locate the resource closer to community members."

plan_quotes.text: Complete design and fund implementation of a community garden in the area to address demand.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: To meet local demand for fresh food options, the 2024 North Laurel - Savage Sustainable Community Plan includes a strategy to "Complete design and fund implementation of a community garden in the area."

plan_quotes.text: Increase capacity, awareness and coordination between local entities that address food insecurity.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key quality of life strategy in the 2024 North Laurel - Savage Sustainable Community Plan is to "Increase capacity, awareness and coordination between local entities that address food insecurity."

plan_areas.community_vision: Howard County is a welcoming and inclusive community that residents are proud to call home. Our collective vision is to accommodate future growth in a manner that retains and improves upon the unique and diverse community character of Howard County. We will continue to support, promote, and act toward creating a community grounded in civility, sustainable development patterns, environmental stewardship, and well-maintained supporting infrastructure. Policies and investments will respect and prioritize the natural environment, historic resources and agricultural heritage, diverse cultures and people, and established community character in an equitable, predictable, sustainable, and achievable way for generations to come.

plan_quotes.text: Some participants advocated for more food options located closer to carless households. Columbia’s walkable village centers were identified as good locations for restaurants and grocery stores featuring locally-sourced food.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The HoCo By Design plan notes a community desire for "more food options located closer to carless households," identifying Columbia’s walkable village centers as good locations for restaurants and grocery stores featuring locally-sourced food.

plan_quotes.text: Use creative solutions to address food deserts (areas without healthy, fresh food options).
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key finding from community focus groups in the HoCo By Design plan is the need to "use creative solutions to address food deserts (areas without healthy, fresh food options)."

plan_quotes.text: Sustainability and food security mean preservation of our local farms and pollinators.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A resident's perspective in the HoCo By Design plan links environmental health to food systems, stating that, "Sustainability and food security mean preservation of our local farms and pollinators."

plan_quotes.text: To ensure underserved populations can participate in training, entities involved in workforce development should partner to offer resources such as child care.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The HoCo By Design plan highlights that to support economic opportunity, "entities involved in workforce development should partner to offer resources such as child care" to ensure underserved populations can participate in training.

Smith Island United exists to represent the Island's interests and provide capacity to move forward on the Smith Island Vision Plan.

plan_quotes.text: In particular, the County has no major shopping center, only modest retail strips and downtown shopping in the two towns, no movie theaters and few restaurants.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 1996 Somerset County Comprehensive Plan highlights the need for expanded retail amenities, observing that, "the County has no major shopping center, only modest retail strips and downtown shopping in the two towns."

plan_quotes.text: By contrast, developments in Salisbury and Wicomico County are better planned, designed as communities, offer internal recreation, day-care and other amenities and offer more stylish homes.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 1996 Somerset County Comprehensive Plan notes that to be competitive, local housing developments could be enhanced with key amenities, observing that developments in neighboring counties, "offer internal recreation, day-care and other amenities and offer more stylish homes."

plan_quotes.text: Limited hours of local restaurants can make it difficult for tourists to find a place to eat in the mornings or evenings.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 Smith Island Sustainable Communities Plan notes that, "Limited hours of local restaurants can make it difficult for tourists to find a place to eat in the mornings or evenings."

plan_quotes.text: Limited attractions, stores, and restaurants; existing establishments have limited hours.

properties.tract_name: The town-center of Hampstead

plan_areas.community_vision: Carroll County is a great place to live, work, and play. The County conserves and promotes its unique rural agricultural heritage, protects its environmental resources, and promotes a balanced approach to new development and economic opportunities consistent with the fabric of its communities. Carroll County values, and citizens’ unalienable rights of life, liberty, and property, are respected, protected, and sustained.

Hampstead is the quintessential American small town. The community is clean, safe and attractive. The residential neighborhoods are quiet and well maintained. While many residents work outside the community, this is “home.” Hampstead is a great place for families. The public schools are excellent and the neighborhoods have very little crime. There are outstanding youth sports programs and a wide range of parks, playgrounds and recreational facilities. Hampstead is an active community. Residents walk, particularly around neighborhoods and on Main Street. While primarily a residential community, Hampstead has a thriving business district. The historic downtown is constantly improving. With many commuters using the Hampstead Bypass, the congestion on Main Street is much reduced. Heavier commercial uses are clustered at the north and south ends of Towns, preserving Hampstead’s “small town” feel. Industrial development is concentrated in and around existing industrial sites. These sites are buffered from the rest of the community. All new construction is held to high standards for design. While large enough to qualify as a “city,” Hampstead is committed to remaining a “town”-- in name and character. It is a community people are proud to call home.
Create a prosperous, vibrant community identity that provides a sense of place and achieves balanced growth all while protecting our unique heritage.

plan_quotes.text: To support our local farmers and to establish a local farmer’s market in the downtown area.

plan_quotes.text: The Hampstead Farmers’ Market is open every Saturday from June to September. The Market can have as many as thirty vendors on a Saturday and the market only allows vendors who grow, make, or bake what they sell. The majority of the vendors are local farms selling their produce, meats and dairy products.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 Hampstead Sustainable Communities Renewal Application highlights access to fresh food options, noting that, "The Hampstead Farmers’ Market is open every Saturday from June to September... the market only allows vendors who grow, make, or bake what they sell. The majority of the vendors are local farms selling their produce, meats and dairy products."

plan_areas.community_vision: IT IS THE YEAR 2040. FREDERICK COUNTY IS A VIBRANT AND UNIQUE COMMUNITY WHERE PEOPLE LIVE, WORK, AND THRIVE WHILE ENJOYING A STRONG SENSE OF PLACE AND BELONGING.

In 2040, Thurmont is a vibrant community with an active downtown where both new and historic buildings are occupied with successful businesses and residents. The Town’s abundant park system is interconnected with new open spaces and trails, and an abundant number of trees are planted throughout the Town. While growing only in a steady, balanced, and well managed way, Thurmont has conserved and protected its unique natural setting at the foot of the Catoctin Mountains. It remains surrounded by farm fields, orchards, and streams, and it has maintained its small-town cozy feel, where citizens help each other and welcome newcomers. Thurmont has succeeded at encouraging new businesses and clean industry, embraced technological advances in telecommunications, and promoted walking, biking, outdoor recreation, and community wide celebrations.
An active and engaged citizenry focused on the well-being of the Town government and more broadly the well-being of the community.

plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes the importance of, "Expanding opportunities for early childhood education programs and services in the county to ensure that all children have access to high quality early educational programs, which are predictors to success later in life."

plan_quotes.text: Increase the food options in the City of Frederick. As an example, in 2019 Parks and Recreation created a farmer's market and food truck event that occurred every Friday during the Summer and Fall.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Patrick Street Corridor plan states a desired outcome is to, "Increase the food options in the City of Frederick," and notes the success of a farmer's market and food truck event.

properties.tract_name: The tract encompassing the neighborhoods of Holly Oaks, Dover Acres, Peach Blossom Heights, Beechwood, Stoney Ridge, South Beechwood, and Clifton

plan_areas.community_vision: The primary goal of Talbot County’s Comprehensive Plan is to promote a high quality of life, to preserve the rural character of our County and to protect the health, safety and well-being of its citizens, in a resilient community.

plan_quotes.text: The location of housing – its proximity to jobs, childcare, stores and services and whether or not these are accessible by car, transit, or walking – also has a significant impact on the cost of living and therefore affordability.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2016 Talbot County Comprehensive Plan notes the importance of housing affordability, highlighting that, "The location of housing – its proximity to jobs, childcare, stores and services...also has a significant impact on the cost of living and therefore affordability."

plan_quotes.text: Nine private schools also enroll students from within and outside the County, including five which enroll only nursery school ages.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2016 Talbot County Comprehensive Plan states that, "Nine private schools also enroll students from within and outside the County, including five which enroll only nursery school ages."

plan_quotes.text: The Office works in cooperation with the County Department of Planning and Zoning on approval and inspection of septic systems and regulation of conditions in trailer parks, foster homes, labor camps and day care facilities.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2016 Talbot County Comprehensive Plan notes that the Office of Environmental Health is involved in regulating conditions in "trailer parks, foster homes, labor camps and day care facilities."

plan_quotes.text: To ensure that affordable housing is practical and suitable, it should be located in close proximity, and with easy access to employment opportunities, social and health services, schools, food markets and other resources affecting the cost of living.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2016 Talbot County Comprehensive Plan highlights that for affordable housing to be practical, "it should be located in close proximity, and with easy access to...food markets and other resources affecting the cost of living."

plan_quotes.text: Families who pay more than 30% of their household income for housing are considered cost burdened and may have difficulty affording necessities such as food, clothing, transportation and medical care.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2016 Talbot County Comprehensive Plan observes that when housing costs are high, families "may have difficulty affording necessities such as food, clothing, transportation and medical care."

plan_quotes.text: The Senior Center also manages the Meals on Wheels program that delivered 17,126 meals to Talbot County residents in fiscal year 2013 and more than 19,000 in 2014.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2016 Talbot County Comprehensive Plan notes a community need for food assistance, stating that one local senior center manages "the Meals on Wheels program that delivered...more than 19,000 in 2014."

plan_quotes.text: ...farm markets, produce stands, wholesale and retail greenhouses, fish and game hatcheries, and riding stables are all permitted uses in agricultural areas.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: To support local food sources, the 2016 Talbot County Comprehensive Plan states that "farm markets, produce stands, wholesale and retail greenhouses...are all permitted uses in agricultural areas."

properties.tract_name: The neighborhood of Orchard Ridge

plan_areas.community_vision: Together, we envision a Baltimore of harmony, inclusivity, and prosperity, where every child has opportunities to thrive no matter what zip code they live in, and residents play an essential role in Baltimore’s thriving future.

The plan's overall goals are to enhance the City’s economic competitiveness, inclusiveness and workforce development; build upon existing strengths, assets and amenities; support transportation efficiency and access; promote access to affordable housing; and leverage and coordinate policies and investments.

plan_quotes.text: In 2021, a Maryland Food Bank survey found that 33% of residents said they were food insecure. This number increased from 27% in 2017.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Our Baltimore, Your Baltimore plan notes that, "In 2021, a Maryland Food Bank survey found that 33% of residents said they were food insecure. This number increased from 27% in 2017."

plan_quotes.text: Many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the 'Black Butterfly', are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Our Baltimore, Your Baltimore plan highlights that, "Many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the ‘Black Butterfly’, are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods."

plan_quotes.text: Community divestment and policy issues also contribute to a lack of food access. This can be in the form of lack of financial investment to support grocery stores or limited or unreliable public transportation making it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key community concern identified in the 2024 Our Baltimore, Your Baltimore plan is that, "Community divestment and policy issues also contribute to a lack of food access. This can be in the form of lack of financial investment to support grocery stores or limited or unreliable public transportation making it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores."

plan_quotes.text: Some neighborhoods have more fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options because the zoning code does not restrict them outright, or the total number located in a particular area.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Our Baltimore, Your Baltimore plan notes that some neighborhoods, "have more fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options."

plan_quotes.text: According to Feeding America, as of 2020, approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Baltimore City Sustainable Community renewal application highlights a significant community need, noting that, "approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects."

plan_quotes.text: Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas, areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key revitalization goal in the 2023 Baltimore City Sustainable Community plan is to "Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas, where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods."

plan_quotes.text: increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms on vacant land.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Baltimore City Sustainable Community plan supports an initiative to "increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms on vacant land."

plan_quotes.text: ...the Purple Line would be extended to the Waverly Giant on East 33rd Street as part of efforts to increase access to fresh food options.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: To improve food access, the 2023 Baltimore City Sustainable Community plan notes that a transit route "would be extended to the Waverly Giant on East 33rd Street as part of efforts to increase access to fresh food options."

plan_quotes.text: Recognizing the need for fresh food access, and the stabilizing force that these markets can have on the neighborhood, the City has proceeded with design planning and/or Requests for Proposals for all of the city-owned markets.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Baltimore City Sustainable Community plan highlights the importance of public markets, stating a commitment based on "Recognizing the need for fresh food access, and the stabilizing force that these markets can have on the neighborhood."

plan_areas.community_vision: livable, healthy communities in harmony with nature—communities that have resilient economies, social equity, and strong regional ties

To revitalize Arbutus into a vibrant 'college town' environment that serves both the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC) and local residents, while protecting the area’s small town charm. The plan focuses on attracting and retaining diverse businesses, improving housing options, and enhancing community health and quality of life through strategic investments and partnerships.

plan_quotes.text: Several communities mention a dearth of grocery stores.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2030 Baltimore County Master Plan notes that, "Several communities mention a dearth of grocery stores."

plan_quotes.text: Liberty Road is a food desert, there are so few locations to acquire fresh food and produce, with such close farmland, the County needs to find ways to get the fresh produce being grown locally sold locally. Perhaps a cooperative?
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key community concern identified in the 2030 Baltimore County Master Plan is that, "Liberty Road is a food desert, there are so few locations to acquire fresh food and produce...the County needs to find ways to get the fresh produce being grown locally sold locally."

plan_quotes.text: Affordable child care vs Pre-K/ Alternatives (funding for one parent to stay home. Affordable Meeting space facilities (Libraries))
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback gathered for the 2030 Baltimore County Master Plan highlights a need to explore options for, "Affordable child care vs Pre-K/ Alternatives (funding for one parent to stay home...)".

plan_quotes.text: Reduce the number of food deserts and promote access to healthy food for all ages, particularly in low/moderate income communities.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2030 Baltimore County Master Plan sets a goal to, "Reduce the number of food deserts and promote access to healthy food for all ages, particularly in low/moderate income communities."

plan_quotes.text: Bring in facilities like day cares, decent shopping center, better grocery stores, good schools and parks to attract young families.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: To support local growth, the 2021 Arbutus Sustainable Community Application notes the importance of attracting young families by helping to "Bring in facilities like day cares... better grocery stores, good schools and parks."

plan_quotes.text: Explore options of higher end grocery stores and cafes similar to Catonsville and Ellicott City.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key economic goal in the 2021 Arbutus Sustainable Community Application is to "Explore options of higher end grocery stores and cafes similar to Catonsville and Ellicott City."

plan_quotes.text: Work with partners including the UMBC, Guinness Brewery, GABA Baltimore County Arts Guild to create and support more outdoor events, health and wellness facility, dog park, farmer’s market, community center, arts and events to cater UMBC students, murals, tourists and bring more amenities to the area.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 Arbutus Sustainable Community Application highlights a strategy to enhance community life and work with partners to create amenities such as a "farmer’s market, community center, arts and events to cater UMBC students, murals, tourists and bring more amenities to the area."

plan_areas.community_vision: In 2035, Prince George’s County is the community of choice for families, businesses, and workers in the region. It is distinguished by strong, green, and healthy communities; a competitive, innovative, and adaptive economy; vibrant and walkable mixed-use centers; quality open space; restored ecosystems; and iconic destinations. It meets the diverse needs of all Prince Georgians and embraces and builds on the momentum generated by new residents, technology, and business opportunities.

plan_quotes.text: Some noted that the costs of childcare and transportation were a barrier to employment as the costs could exceed participants’ earning potential.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2014 Plan Prince George's 2035 notes that for some residents, "the costs of childcare and transportation were a barrier to employment as the costs could exceed participants’ earning potential."

plan_quotes.text: Promote healthy lifestyles by ensuring access to healthy foods, health services, and a network of trails, parks, and recreational opportunities.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2014 Plan Prince George's 2035 outlines a vision for healthy communities that, "Promote healthy lifestyles by ensuring access to healthy foods, health services, and a network of trails, parks, and recreational opportunities."

plan_quotes.text: Approximately 100,000 County residents lived in food deserts in 2010, defined as low-income census tracts where a significant share or number of residents are more than one mile (in urban settings) or ten miles (in rural settings) from the nearest supermarket.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2014 Plan Prince George's 2035 notes a key challenge is that, "Approximately 100,000 County residents lived in food deserts in 2010, defined as low-income census tracts where a significant share or number of residents are more than one mile (in urban settings) or ten miles (in rural settings) from the nearest supermarket."

plan_quotes.text: The majority of food deserts (approximately 73 percent) are concentrated inside the Capital Beltway.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2014 Plan Prince George's 2035 notes that, "The majority of food deserts (approximately 73 percent) are concentrated inside the Capital Beltway."

plan_quotes.text: 71 percent of all restaurants in Prince George’s County were classified in 2012 as fast food.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key community health concern identified in the 2014 Plan Prince George's 2035 is that, "71 percent of all restaurants in Prince George’s County were classified in 2012 as fast food."

plan_quotes.text: Several communities mention a dearth of grocery stores.

plan_quotes.text: Liberty Road is a food desert, there are so few locations to acquire fresh food and produce, with such close farmland, the County needs to find ways to get the fresh produce being grown locally sold locally. Perhaps a cooperative?

plan_areas.community_vision: Thrive Montgomery 2050 aims to create communities that offer equitable access to jobs, more housing, transportation, parks, and public spaces. plan_quotes.text: As the county plans for the future, it should continue to find ways to address the specific needs of the vulnerable populations impacted by the hidden costs of poverty and determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation.

plan_areas.community_vision: Together, we envision a Baltimore of harmony, inclusivity, and prosperity, where every child has opportunities to thrive no matter what zip code they live in, and residents play an essential role in Baltimore’s thriving future.

The plan's overall goals are to enhance the City’s economic competitiveness, inclusiveness and workforce development; build upon existing strengths, assets and amenities; support transportation efficiency and access; promote access to affordable housing; and leverage and coordinate policies and investments.

plan_quotes.text: In 2021, a Maryland Food Bank survey found that 33% of residents said they were food insecure. This number increased from 27% in 2017.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Our Baltimore, Your Baltimore plan notes that, "In 2021, a Maryland Food Bank survey found that 33% of residents said they were food insecure. This number increased from 27% in 2017."

plan_quotes.text: Many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the 'Black Butterfly', are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Our Baltimore, Your Baltimore plan highlights that, "Many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the ‘Black Butterfly’, are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods."

plan_quotes.text: Community divestment and policy issues also contribute to a lack of food access. This can be in the form of lack of financial investment to support grocery stores or limited or unreliable public transportation making it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key community concern identified in the 2024 Our Baltimore, Your Baltimore plan is that, "Community divestment and policy issues also contribute to a lack of food access. This can be in the form of lack of financial investment to support grocery stores or limited or unreliable public transportation making it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores."

plan_quotes.text: Some neighborhoods have more fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options because the zoning code does not restrict them outright, or the total number located in a particular area.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Our Baltimore, Your Baltimore plan notes that some neighborhoods, "have more fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options."

plan_quotes.text: According to Feeding America, as of 2020, approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Baltimore City Sustainable Community renewal application highlights a significant community need, noting that, "approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects."

plan_quotes.text: Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas, areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key revitalization goal in the 2023 Baltimore City Sustainable Community plan is to "Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas, where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods."

plan_quotes.text: increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms on vacant land.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Baltimore City Sustainable Community plan supports an initiative to "increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms on vacant land."

plan_quotes.text: ...the Purple Line would be extended to the Waverly Giant on East 33rd Street as part of efforts to increase access to fresh food options.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: To improve food access, the 2023 Baltimore City Sustainable Community plan notes that a transit route "would be extended to the Waverly Giant on East 33rd Street as part of efforts to increase access to fresh food options."

plan_quotes.text: Recognizing the need for fresh food access, and the stabilizing force that these markets can have on the neighborhood, the City has proceeded with design planning and/or Requests for Proposals for all of the city-owned markets.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Baltimore City Sustainable Community plan highlights the importance of public markets, stating a commitment based on "Recognizing the need for fresh food access, and the stabilizing force that these markets can have on the neighborhood."

plan_quotes.text: In 2021, a Maryland Food Bank survey found that 33% of residents said they were food insecure. This number increased from 27% in 2017.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Our Baltimore, Your Baltimore plan notes that, "In 2021, a Maryland Food Bank survey found that 33% of residents said they were food insecure. This number increased from 27% in 2017."

plan_quotes.text: Many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the 'Black Butterfly', are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Our Baltimore, Your Baltimore plan highlights that, "Many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the ‘Black Butterfly’, are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods."

plan_quotes.text: Community divestment and policy issues also contribute to a lack of food access. This can be in the form of lack of financial investment to support grocery stores or limited or unreliable public transportation making it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key community concern identified in the 2024 Our Baltimore, Your Baltimore plan is that, "Community divestment and policy issues also contribute to a lack of food access. plan_quotes.text: Some neighborhoods have more fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options because the zoning code does not restrict them outright, or the total number located in a particular area.

plan_quotes.text: Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas, areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.

plan_quotes.text: ...the Purple Line would be extended to the Waverly Giant on East 33rd Street as part of efforts to increase access to fresh food options.

plan_quotes.text: Recognizing the need for fresh food access, and the stabilizing force that these markets can have on the neighborhood, the City has proceeded with design planning and/or Requests for Proposals for all of the city-owned markets.

plan_areas.community_vision: livable, healthy communities in harmony with nature—communities that have resilient economies, social equity, and strong regional ties

The Sustainable Community Action Plan is a multi-year investment strategy – a strategic set of revitalization initiatives and projects that local partners believe will increase the economic vitality and livability of their community, increase prosperity for local households and improve the health of the surrounding environment.

plan_quotes.text: Several communities mention a dearth of grocery stores.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2030 Baltimore County Master Plan notes that, "Several communities mention a dearth of grocery stores."

plan_quotes.text: Liberty Road is a food desert, there are so few locations to acquire fresh food and produce, with such close farmland, the County needs to find ways to get the fresh produce being grown locally sold locally. Perhaps a cooperative?
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: A key community concern identified in the 2030 Baltimore County Master Plan is that, "Liberty Road is a food desert, there are so few locations to acquire fresh food and produce...the County needs to find ways to get the fresh produce being grown locally sold locally."

plan_quotes.text: Affordable child care vs Pre-K/ Alternatives (funding for one parent to stay home. Affordable Meeting space facilities (Libraries))
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback gathered for the 2030 Baltimore County Master Plan highlights a need to explore options for, "Affordable child care vs Pre-K/ Alternatives (funding for one parent to stay home...)".

plan_quotes.text: Reduce the number of food deserts and promote access to healthy food for all ages, particularly in low/moderate income communities.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2030 Baltimore County Master Plan sets a goal to, "Reduce the number of food deserts and promote access to healthy food for all ages, particularly in low/moderate income communities."

plan_quotes.text: Continue efforts to work with brokers and developers to address the need of quality grocery stores and upscale restaurants in the Liberty Road area.
plan_quotes.briefing_quote: The 2020 Northwest Gateways Sustainable Community Action Plan Update highlights a strategy to, "Continue efforts to work with brokers and developers to address the need of quality grocery stores and upscale restaurants in the Liberty Road area."
